字数 vs 词数

这两个词在中文和英文里指向不同的东西：

  • 字数（characters）：每个字符（汉字、字母、数字、标点）都算一个。中文里习惯把「字数」理解为「字符数」，1 个汉字 = 1 个字符。
  • 词数（words）：连续的字母或数字串算一个词。英文里 1 个单词 = 1 个词；中文里如果按词切分，「今天天气真好」是 4 个词（今天/天气/真/好）。

主流工具的处理方式：

语言主指标辅助指标
中文字数（字符数）句数、段数
英文词数（words）句数、段数
混排两者并看阅读时长

本站 字数统计器 会同时显示字符数、中文字数、英文词数、句数、段数，避免混排文本被误判。

中英文的计算方式

中文字数怎么数

主流约定：Unicode CJK 统一汉字区段（U+4E00–U+9FFF）加扩展 A 区段（U+3400–U+4DBF）都算汉字。中文标点（，。！？；：""''…）和英文标点都不算「汉字」，但会计入「总字符数」。

常见的边界情况：

  • 全角/半角：全角字母（ＡＢＣ）按汉字算，半角（ABC）按英文词算——这会造成统计不一致，建议统一用半角。
  • 繁体字：繁体（漢字）也在 CJK 区段内，正常计入。
  • 标点：中文字数里标点不计入，所以 100 字的文章实际可能是 110 字符。

英文词数怎么数

主流规则：连续的字母或数字串算一个词，支持缩写（Mary's = 1 词）、数字（3.14 = 1 词、1,000 = 1 词）、连字符（well-known = 1 词或 2 词，看工具）。中文标点不影响英文词的判定——「Hello，world」仍然是 2 个词。

混排

「今天发布新 product！」按主流规则：中文 4 个字符（今天发布新）+ 英文 1 个词（product）+ 1 个感叹号。这类文本应分别报两个数字，再用阅读时长合并。

阅读与朗读速度的依据

「读一篇文章要多久」是用字数除以速度得出的。速度基准来自研究数据：

场景中文速度英文速度依据
阅读≈ 400 字/分钟≈ 200-300 词/分钟成人平均速度，阅读能力强的可到 400-500 wpm
朗读≈ 220 字/分钟≈ 150 词/分钟新闻播报级，清晰但自然
演讲≈ 180 字/分钟≈ 130 词/分钟舞台演讲，留停顿

这些是基准值，实际因人而异：复杂内容（学术、法律）速度慢 30-50%；简单内容（儿童读物、口语体）可快 30%。工具给出的时间是估算，供参考不供考核。

不同文体的字数差异

同样是「一篇文章」，不同文体的目标字数天差地别：

文体中文目标英文目标说明
新闻快讯200-500 字150-300 词短平快，1 分钟读完
微博/短推140-300 字140 字符社交平台硬上限
博客长文2000-5000 字1000-2500 词SEO 友好区间
学术论文8000-15000 字5000-10000 词含参考文献
演讲稿1500-3000 字1000-2000 词8-15 分钟演讲量
说明书3000-8000 字1500-4000 词结构清晰、段落短
小说章节3000-6000 字2000-4000 词按章节节奏

写作前先定目标字数，写完后核对差距。差距过大通常是结构问题——不是补字就是删字，而是重新分配段落权重。

常见写作目标的字数

社交平台

  • 微信公众号：正文 800-2000 字为宜；标题 10-30 字；摘要 40-80 字。
  • 知乎回答：干货回答 500-2000 字；深度分析可到 5000 字。
  • 小红书：正文 300-800 字；标题 10-20 字。
  • Twitter/X：140 字符（英文约 28-35 词）；长文要拆推文串。

写作与学术

  • 论文摘要：200-300 词（英文）；中文约 400-600 字。
  • 论文正文：本科 5000-15000 字；硕士 20000-50000 字；博士 50000+ 字。
  • 邮件正文：30-200 字，长邮件分点列出。

演讲稿

8-15 分钟演讲对应中文 1500-3000 字、英文 1000-2000 词。留 10-15% 缓冲（现场会超时）。

SEO 中的字数考量

Google 官方明确说过：没有硬性字数要求。但实际数据支持「内容深度」和排名的相关性：

  • 博客长文：排名靠前的页面中位数约 1000-1500 英文词（约 2000-3000 中文字）。
  • 程序化页面（如本站的工具页）：字数少没关系，但要有结构化数据（JSON-LD）和语义清晰的标题。
  • 指南/教程：越接近「读者要解决的实际问题」越重要，字数是信号不是目标。

常见误区：

  • 为凑字数灌水：会稀释内容密度，反而降低排名。SEO 看的是「信息量/字符」的比率，不是字符数本身。
  • 只看英文词数：中文内容用英文词数判断，会严重低估深度。
  • 忽略结构化数据：字数达标但缺 JSON-LD，Google Rich Results 无法识别，富摘要机会丢失。

正确做法：先定读者要解决的问题，再按文体经验值写；写完后核对字数是否覆盖了问题，而不是反过来用字数反推内容。

常见问题

Q：字数和词数有什么区别？

A：字数按字符计（中文每个汉字算一个字符）；词数按连续字母或数字串计（英文每个单词算一个词）。中文写作用字数，英文写作用词数；混排文本需要同时看两个数字。

Q：阅读速度真的能到 400 字/分钟吗？

A：成人英文阅读平均 200-300 wpm，阅读能力强的可到 400-500 wpm；中文阅读速度约 400 字/分钟是常见估算值。实际速度因文体、复杂度、读者背景差异很大。

Q：SEO 对字数有硬性要求吗？

A：没有硬性要求。Google 官方声明不要求特定字数。但实际数据显示，排名靠前的页面中位数约 1000-1500 词。字数只是内容深度的信号之一。

Q：中文标点算字数吗？

A：主流约定：中文标点计入「总字符数」但不计入「中文字数」，因为标点是符号不是汉字。英文标点和空格同理。

Q：写作时应该以哪个数字为目标？

A：中文写作以字数为目标，英文写作以词数为目标，混排文本以阅读时长为目标。字数/词数是「量」的指标，阅读时长是「体验」的指标。

Characters vs Words

These two terms point to different things across Chinese and English:

  • Characters (字数): each character (Chinese, Latin letter, digit, punctuation) counts as one. In Chinese, 1 汉字 = 1 character.
  • Words (词数): a run of letters or digits counts as one. In English, 1 word = 1 word; in Chinese, if segmented, "今天天气真好" is 4 words (今天/天气/真/好).

How mainstream tools handle this:

LanguagePrimary metricSecondary
ChineseCharactersSentences, paragraphs
EnglishWordsSentences, paragraphs
MixedBothReading time

Our Word Counter shows character count, Chinese characters, English words, sentences, and paragraphs side-by-side, so mixed text isn't misread.

Counting Rules for Chinese & English

How Chinese characters are counted

Standard convention: the CJK Unified Ideographs range (U+4E00–U+9FFF) plus Extension A (U+3400–U+4DBF) are counted as Chinese characters. Chinese punctuation (，。！？；：""''…) and English punctuation are not counted as characters, but they do count toward total characters.

Common edge cases:

  • Full-width vs half-width: full-width letters (ＡＢＣ) are treated as Chinese; half-width (ABC) as English. Inconsistent counting results if you mix them — use half-width uniformly.
  • Traditional Chinese: traditional characters (漢字) are in the CJK range, counted normally.
  • Punctuation: Chinese punctuation is excluded from character count, so a 100-character article may actually be 110 characters total.

How English words are counted

Mainstream rule: a run of letters or digits counts as one word. Supports abbreviations (Mary's = 1 word), numbers (3.14 = 1 word, 1,000 = 1 word), hyphenated compounds (well-known = 1 or 2 depending on the tool). Chinese punctuation does not affect English word detection — "Hello，world" is still 2 words.

Mixed text

"今天发布新 product！" under the mainstream rule: 5 Chinese characters (今天发布新) + 1 English word (product) + 1 exclamation. Report both numbers separately, then combine via reading time.

Reading & Speaking Speeds

"How long will it take to read?" is characters divided by speed. Baselines from research:

ScenarioChineseEnglishBasis
Reading~400 chars/min~200-300 wpmAdult average; fast readers 400-500 wpm
Speaking~220 chars/min~150 wpmNews broadcast pace, clear and natural
Presenting~180 chars/min~130 wpmStage speech, with pauses

These are baselines; actual speed varies: complex content (academic, legal) is 30-50% slower; simple content (children's reading, conversational) can be 30% faster. Tool outputs are estimates, for reference not for evaluation.

Genre-Based Lengths

Same "article" can mean wildly different lengths by genre:

GenreChinese targetEnglish targetNotes
News brief200-500 chars150-300 wordsQuick read, 1 minute
Social post140-300 chars140 charsPlatform hard limit
Blog post2000-5000 chars1000-2500 wordsSEO-friendly range
Academic paper8000-15000 chars5000-10000 wordsIncluding references
Speech1500-3000 chars1000-2000 words8-15 minute talk
Manual / docs3000-8000 chars1500-4000 wordsClear structure, short paragraphs
Fiction chapter3000-6000 chars2000-4000 wordsPaced per chapter

Decide a target length before writing, then check the gap afterward. A large gap is usually a structure problem — not more words or fewer, but re-allocated section weight.

Common Writing Targets

Social platforms

  • WeChat Official Account: 800-2000 characters for body; title 10-30 characters; summary 40-80 characters.
  • Zhihu answer: 500-2000 characters for dry-goods; 5000 characters for deep analysis.
  • Xiaohongshu: 300-800 characters for body; title 10-20 characters.
  • Twitter/X: 140 characters (~28-35 English words); long content uses threads.

Writing and academia

  • Paper abstract: 200-300 words (English); ~400-600 Chinese characters.
  • Thesis body: undergraduate 5000-15000 chars; master's 20000-50000 chars; PhD 50000+ chars.
  • Email body: 30-200 characters; long emails should be bulleted.

Speeches

An 8-15 minute talk corresponds to 1500-3000 Chinese characters, or 1000-2000 English words. Leave a 10-15% buffer (live events tend to overrun).

Word Count in SEO

Google has explicitly stated: there is no hard word-count requirement. But actual data supports a correlation between content depth and rankings:

  • Blog posts: top-ranking pages median about 1000-1500 English words (~2000-3000 Chinese characters).
  • Programmatic pages (like our tool pages): short text is fine, provided there's structured data (JSON-LD) and semantically clear titles.
  • Guides/tutorials: being close to "the actual problem the reader wants to solve" matters more; word count is a signal, not a goal.

Common mistakes:

  • Padding to hit a target: dilutes information density and actually lowers rankings. SEO cares about the "information per character" ratio, not raw character count.
  • Reading English word count for Chinese content: severely underestimates depth.
  • Skipping structured data: word count is fine but without JSON-LD, Google Rich Results can't recognize it — missed rich-snippet opportunity.

Right approach: start from the problem the reader wants solved, then write at the genre's typical length; afterward, verify the word count actually covers the problem — don't reverse-engineer content from a word target.

FAQ

Q: What's the difference between characters and words?

A: Characters count each char (Chinese = 1 char per 汉字); words count runs of letters/digits (English word = 1 word). Chinese writing uses character count, English uses word count; mixed text needs both.

Q: Can reading speed really reach 400 chars/min?

A: Adult English reading averages 200-300 wpm, fast readers 400-500 wpm; Chinese reading at ~400 chars/min is a common estimate. Actual speed varies greatly by genre, complexity, and reader background.

Q: Is there a hard SEO word-count requirement?

A: No hard requirement. Google officially states no specific word count is required. Actual data shows top-ranking pages median around 1000-1500 words. Word count is only one signal of content depth.

Q: Does Chinese punctuation count toward word count?

A: Mainstream convention: Chinese punctuation counts toward "total characters" but not "Chinese character count", because punctuation is a symbol not a 汉字. English punctuation and spaces behave similarly.

Q: Which number should I target while writing?

A: Target character count for Chinese, word count for English, reading time for mixed text. Character/word count measures "quantity"; reading time measures "experience".
